chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Among what Musa (peace be upon him) whispered to his Lord was that he said: 'O Lord! What is for the one who comforts the bereaved?' He said: 'I shall shade him in My Shade on the Day there is no shade except My Shade.'

key_terms.الثَّكْلَى: the bereaved (specifically one who has lost a child or parent)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for comforting the bereaved according to the hadith of Musa (AS)?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on condolences, this *hadith qudsi* highlights the spiritual merit of comforting the bereaved by linking it to the eschatological promise of divine protection. In Shia tradition, this narration underscores the social obligation of *ta'ziyah* (condolence), promising that those who alleviate grief will find refuge in Allah's unique shade on the Day of Judgment when all other sources of shade vanish.
